blocks.text: WARSAW, Poland — Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte on Saturday pledged to defend Poland after Russian missiles landed in the country, as the alliance’s top decision-making body prepared to discuss the incident. Warsaw said two Russian missiles struck its southeast on Friday, accusing the Kremlin of “intentional provocation” near an area where thousands of European troops are conducting exercises. Rutte, during a visit to Warsaw, said the alliance would determine what happened to identify any vulnerabilities and pledged to defend Polish territory in remarks to Polish media.
